onboard.title: Erste Schritte
onboard.tip1: keep / maybe / cull setzen und automatisch weiter (~1-2 s je Bild; ⏩ schaltet ab)

toast.disagree_mode_blocked: Deine Filter verbergen alle Abweichungen — entfernen oder erneut klicken zum Beenden
toast.disagree_cleared: Abweichungsprüfung fertig ✓ — deine Urteile sind im Korrektursatz
toast.compare_added: Zum Vergleich hinzugefügt: {n} · Enter zum Öffnen, Esc zum Leeren
compare.modal.title: A/B-Vergleich ({n})
compare.modal.meta: Nach score_final sortiert; links ist die Systemwahl. „Diese wählen" cullt den Rest.
filter.scene_unknown_hint: Photos the scene classifier could not place
card.rotate_title: Rotate 90° clockwise (fine-tune it in the lightbox)
card.compare_title: Pick this frame for A/B compare (Shift+click a thumbnail does the same; c also works)
card.review_me_title: auto / trained model / VLM / DeepSeek disagree on this frame ({n} ★ stddev) — worth a human look
workspace.resolve_maybes_title: Only the maybes, most-ambiguous first — start with the hardest, judge each with 1/2/3
workspace.disagree_review_title: Only frames where the model and the rule stack disagree, most confident split first — these are the most useful corrections
workspace.rescorer_title: V1.1 learned rescorer: keep/maybe predictions on {n} non-cull frames
workspace.human_labels_title: Human rubric labelling progress; these labels train the next rescorer
workspace.active_learning_title: Active-learning queue: the {n} frames most worth labelling — frames where the rules and the rescorer disagree, borderline probabilities, borderline scores, and anything not yet labelled
workspace.all_done_title: Every frame has a human decision — click to download the XMP zip and take the result back to Lightroom
workspace.unreviewed_title: Frames with no human decision yet (keys 1/2/3, the lightbox and bulk selection all count). At zero this becomes the XMP export entry
workspace.tuned_badge: Every keep/cull correction teaches PixCull your taste — {n} more frames and the next batch is calibrated to your standard
workspace.adaptive_band: v0.13.8 self-tuned: keep ≥ {keep} · cull < {cull} (25/75 quantiles over {n} rated frames).\nThis run's score distribution sits ≥ 0.03 away from the global default, so the thresholds are adapted.
grid.burst_peak_title: {bursts} burst groups, {photos} photos — keep only the best frame from each
grid.burst_collapse_title: Collapse each burst to one peak frame plus a ⧉ count; click the ⧉N in the card corner to expand and compare side by side
grid.burst_compare_title: Open side-by-side compare, starting at the first burst group; ←/→ pages
grid.neardup_title: Fold visually similar frames (CLIP) into one representative; click the ≈N in the card corner to compare side by side. The first switch builds an index, so it is slower
grid.scenes_title: Cut the shoot into scenes by capture time; click a scene to jump to that stretch. A narrative flow, not a flat grid
annotation.rationale_placeholder: Why this score? (optional, but more is more useful · type / for commands)
annotation.queue_done: Every frame in this batch is labelled ✓
health.open: Open this to see which stages degraded on this run
health.title: Health of this run
health.note: "Fell back" means the stage ran but used a fallback result; "not attempted" means the stage never ran under this configuration. They are not the same, so they are counted apart.
health.fault: A stage did none of its job
health.degraded: Degraded this run ({degraded} fell back / {withheld} not attempted)
health.mismatch: the screen says {a}, the file says {b} ({c})
tip.title: The AI you can see
tip.row.organise: Left rail, Organise · Fold: ≈ Near-duplicate fold plus the similarity slider. Drag it and watch how the AI groups near-identical frames (adjustable, not a black box)
tip.row.scenes: 🎬 Scenes: cuts the shoot into narrative stretches by capture time
tip.row.why: Open any photo; 🔍 Why at the top explains in one line why it is keep / maybe / cull
